title: Fast & Faithful Function Vectors
abstract: Function vectors (FVs) are task representations elicited during in-context learning that can be used to steer Large Language Models (LLMs). However, design choices in their formulation remain underexplored. In this work, we study the impact of varying FV definitions for instructions along two degrees of freedom: attention head selection and steering. For head selection, using gradient-based attributions with Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) substantially improves efficiency as well as accuracy. For FV steering, applying it in a distributed manner yields a higher accuracy compared to simple aggregation. Our code is publicly available.

significance.justification: The paper provides practical improvements to function vectors that could influence how builders implement in-context learning steering techniques, with measurable gains in efficiency and accuracy.

novelty.justification: While building on existing function vector research, the paper introduces novel variations using gradient-based attributions and distributed steering that represent clear but incremental advances.

reproducibility.justification: The authors state that their code is publicly available, though the abstract doesn't specify the completeness of datasets or implementation details.

clarity.justification: The abstract clearly states the research focus, methods (LRP for head selection, distributed steering), and key findings (improved efficiency and accuracy) with appropriate scope.

topical_fit.justification: Directly addresses LLM steering techniques for in-context learning, which is highly relevant for builders working with function vectors and model control.
